title: Candle Psychology
hook: Going deeper. What specific candle behavior means for your next read.

launchpad.outcome: Explain why two similar-looking candles at the same level can tell opposite stories.
launchpad.missionQuestion: If two candles wick to nearly the same low at support, does that mean they end the same way?

slides.kicker: Every candle is a buyer and seller battle
slides.body:
Buyers push price up. Sellers push price down. The candle close shows who held control by the end of that candle.

I'm not just asking if the candle is green or red. I'm asking where it reacted, where it rejected, and where it closed.

slides.title: Tap each candle to see who actually won
slides.body: Price comes into support and wicks down on both — but the close tells two very different stories.

candles.label: Closed above support
candles.desc: Buyers stepped in and defended the level — the wick tested support, but the close held above it.

candles.label: Closed below support
candles.desc: Sellers actually broke the level — this candle wicked down similarly, but the close settled below support, confirming the break.

slides.kicker: Are they telling the same story?
slides.body: Two candles form at the same support level with nearly identical wicks, but one closes above support and the other closes below it.

check.prompt: Are they telling the same story?

options.label: No — one shows buyers defending the level, the other shows sellers actually breaking it
options.why: Right — reading only the wick would make two very different events look the same.

options.label: Yes — similar wicks always mean the same outcome
options.feedback: The close is what separates "defended" from "failed."

slides.quote: I'm not just asking if the candle is green or red. I'm asking where it reacted, where it rejected, and where it closed.

slides.body: The close is what confirms whether a level actually held or broke.

check.prompt: Before calling acceptance above a level, wait for the candle ___.

options.label: Close
options.why: The close is what confirms acceptance, not the wick or the color.

options.label: Color
options.feedback: Color alone doesn't confirm acceptance — the close does.

options.label: Volume spike
options.feedback: Volume can add context, but the close is what actually confirms the level held or broke.

slides.prompt: Imagine another AGHF member asks: "If two candles have almost the same wick, why would you read them differently?" How would you explain it to them?
slides.modelAnswer: Because the wick only shows where price visited — it doesn't decide the outcome. The close is what actually separates a defended level from a broken one. Two candles can wick to nearly the same low and still tell opposite stories, depending on where each one actually closed.

takeaways: Buyers and sellers fight inside every candle — the close shows who won.
Similar wicks can hide opposite outcomes — the close is the tiebreaker.
Read where price reacted, rejected, and closed — not just its color.
remember: It's not green or red. It's where it closed.
